title: Plan-level state (context/project/plans/<plan-id>/state.yaml)
description: Mutable execution state for one plan: per-wave and per-story status, retry counts, worktree refs (per story and per retry attempt), validation + conformance results, and rough telemetry. mexecute reads/writes this to drive resume, retry, and progress. Distinct from the immutable plan.yaml graph.

version.description: New state files are written with 4. Earlier versions still resolve: no field was ever renamed, and an absent slices[] reads as one implicit slice covering every wave.

run.description: The run counter for this plan. 0 means never executed and is the value mplan seeds into a fresh state file. mexecute increments it once per invocation, over the whole plan, so the first invocation runs as 1. The increment is unconditional — identical on a fresh plan and on a resume.

integration_branches.description: Per-repo integration branch: greens merge here (not the repo's live working branch).

slices.description: One entry per graph slice, written by mship through mc.py state set-slice. Absent on a pre-slice plan, which is read as one implicit slice covering every wave. Slice-level resumption derives from these statuses; resume_wave is unchanged and still names a wave.

conformance.description: Result of the Step 3 /mverify sweep. Written by the mexecute session from the sweep's returned result once the Workflow returns (no barrier remains by then); written by mverify itself only on a standalone run.

report.description: Path to the mverify report under context/project/out/.

deferred.description: Findings mfix deliberately accepted as debt. check handoff subtracts this from findings before deciding whether a plan still has conformance work outstanding, which is what lets a legitimately deferred finding stop pinning the check at error indefinitely. Absent means 0, so every existing conformance block keeps its current meaning.

telemetry.description: Rough actuals for the run (never a pre-run estimate).

acceptance.description: unconfirmed is the --gate never case: a slice whose acceptance could only be judged by a person, run with nobody to ask. It is deliberately neither pass nor fail, so a report cannot present an unlooked-at slice as demonstrated.

outcome.description: mship's decision at this slice boundary; null until the slice is decided.

armed.description: The exit code of the slice's surface: delivered acceptance command, run BEFORE the slice's stories. It must be non-zero: an acceptance that already passes either does not reach the behaviour the slice delivers or the slice delivers nothing. mc.py state set-slice --armed refuses 0, so this field can only ever hold a red. Its presence is what makes the later green a demonstration rather than a claim.

confirmed.description: The exit code of the same command, re-run after the slice's last barrier. mc.py state set-slice refuses --confirmed non-zero paired with --acceptance pass, and refuses --confirmed at all on a slice that was never armed.

run.description: The run this attempt belongs to. An attempt always belongs to a started run, so unlike the top-level counter it is never 0.

worktree.description: Worktree path; null once removed after a green merge.

worktree_removed.description: true once a merged (green) worktree is cleaned up; failed/unmerged worktrees are kept.

retries.description: Attempts made so far (bounded auto-retry N=3).

merged_branch.description: The integration branch the green attempt merged into, or null.

contract_revisions.description: Shared interface TAG -> the agreement revision this story was built against, recorded at merge. Absent means the story consumed no shared interface. A later cascade that bumps a revision above the one recorded here is what makes the story's code a stale-contract-revision finding.

deferred_break.description: A contained breaking-contract change deferred to the final report (did not halt the run).
